panels.description: Minimum readiness across selected instances. BAD means at least one exporter has not started all registered monitors.
panels.title: Exporter Ready

panels.description: Minimum hl-node/hl-visor process state across selected instances.
panels.title: Node Processes

panels.description: Absent until both version probes have succeeded. BAD means at least one selected node is outdated.
panels.title: Software Current

panels.description: Actual filesystem utilization from statfs. This is not NODE_HOME size divided by filesystem size.
panels.title: Filesystem Used

panels.description: Worst age of the latest HyperCore block among selected instances.
panels.title: Core Block Age

panels.description: Worst age of the latest HyperEVM block. No data when EVM monitoring is disabled.
panels.title: EVM Block Age

panels.description: Worst reference-node lag, only for visor samples that actually contain reference_lag.
panels.title: Reference Lag

panels.description: Worst time since a periodic ABCI snapshot completed successfully.
panels.title: Snapshot Age

panels.description: Local applied heights. HyperCore tracks the fast state in dual-state mode; visor is the applied ABCI height; EVM uses its own height domain.
panels.title: Block Heights

panels.description: Difference in blocks between each selected node and the highest visor height in the same environment. This is fleet-relative, not an authoritative network height.

targets.expr: max by (env) (hl_visor_height{env=~"$env", instance=~"$instance"}) - on(env) group_right hl_visor_height{env=~"$env", instance=~"$instance"}

panels.title: Fleet Height Lag

panels.description: Age of the newest visor state sample. Growth means the local sync-state feed stopped updating even if the last height remains visible.
panels.title: Visor Observation Age

panels.description: Wall-clock ages for core/EVM blocks and visor observations. Reference lag is included only when populated by hl-visor.
panels.title: Block And Sync Age

panels.description: consensus_time minus local wall clock. Positive means chain time is ahead; negative means the local node sees stale chain time or has clock skew.
panels.title: Consensus Clock Offset

panels.description: Fast checkpoint height minus slow checkpoint height. Positive values mean the slow EVM database tier is behind.
panels.title: EVM Checkpoint Tier Lag

panels.description: p50 and p95 from the block-time histogram. Values are milliseconds and remain separated by state_type when dual-state data is present.
panels.title: Core Block Time

panels.description: Per-block gasUsed/gasLimit, converted from a 0..1 fraction to percent.
panels.title: EVM Gas Utilization

panels.description: Rates of HyperCore transactions/orders and EVM transaction types. Requires replica metrics for HyperCore series and EVM metrics for EVM series.
panels.title: Chain Throughput

panels.description: Aggregate gossip-connection events by sanitized type. Spikes in stream checks, greetings or errors indicate connection churn; verified_gossip_rpc is the request/handshake arrival signal.
panels.title: Gossip Event Rate

panels.description: Per-IP verified gossip-RPC volume over ten minutes. A fixed 10-second pull loop is approximately 60 events per ten minutes.

targets.expr: topk(25, sum by (instance, ip) (increase(hl_p2p_gossip_peer_events_total{env=~"$env", instance=~"$instance", event_type="verified_gossip_rpc"}[10m]))) > 0

panels.title: Top Gossip RPC Peers (10m)

panels.description: Combined per-IP stream setup, checking, greeting and connection-error events. Use Loki to inspect exact sub-second cadence and payloads.
panels.title: Reconnect And Handshake Spam (10m)

panels.description: Remote IPs producing gossip activity on more than one selected node. Select multiple instances to detect coordinated multi-node behavior.
panels.title: Coordinated IPs Across Nodes (10m)

panels.description: Percentage of gossip events whose structured JSON payload had no valid IP field. A high value means Loki is required for attribution or the parser needs another structured field variant.

targets.expr: 100 * sum by (instance) (rate(hl_p2p_gossip_events_unattributed_total{env=~"$env", instance=~"$instance"}[10m])) / clamp_min(sum by (instance) (rate(hl_p2p_gossip_events_total{env=~"$env", instance=~"$instance"}[10m])), 0.000001)

panels.title: Unattributed Gossip Share

panels.description: Per-IP outbound compressed-byte growth. This is the strongest available traffic-side signal for peers pulling blocks/state. Gauge resets are clamped to zero.

targets.expr: topk(25, sum by (instance, ip) (clamp_min(delta(hl_p2p_lz4_bytes_total{env=~"$env", instance=~"$instance", direction="out", ip!="other"}[10m]), 0))) > 0

panels.title: Top Outbound Compressed Data (10m)

panels.description: Latest raw tcp_traffic values by IP and direction. Values are comparative node-native rates, not bytes. Only the top 16 peers per direction are individually exposed.
panels.title: Top Peer Traffic Snapshot

panels.description: Historical effective parent peer, inferred as the inbound IP delivering the most traffic. Resolution is bounded by source sampling and Prometheus scrape intervals.
panels.title: Parent Peer Timeline

panels.description: Raw inbound tcp_traffic attributed to the currently inferred parent. Comparative only, not bytes.
panels.title: Parent Peer Traffic

panels.description: Time the current inferred parent has continuously held the role since the exporter observed the last switch.
panels.title: Parent Tenure

panels.description: Current active peers, sampled directional peers, rolling unique IPs, and current non-validator gossip peers use different denominators and are intentionally shown separately.
panels.title: Peer Counts

panels.description: Total raw hl-node tcp_traffic value by direction. Useful for relative changes only; this is not byte throughput.
panels.title: Aggregate P2P Traffic

panels.description: New peer registrations and LRU/TTL evictions over ten minutes. Sustained additions indicate discovery churn or connection scanning.
panels.title: Peer Churn (10m)

panels.description: Linux TCP state counts on Hyperliquid P2P ports. Rising TIME_WAIT/SYN states can expose reconnect storms or connection pressure.
panels.title: TCP Connection States

panels.description: Age since each known IP was last observed through traffic or structured gossip. Requires --per-peer-metrics; lower values are more recent.
panels.title: Recently Seen Peer IPs

panels.description: Node-precomputed per-instance p95 gauges. topk selects the currently slowest subsystem series; do not aggregate these quantiles across nodes.
panels.title: Slowest Subsystems P95

panels.description: Percent of wall-clock time spent doing work per subsystem. This is a duty cycle, not latency.
panels.title: Subsystem Work Fraction

panels.description: p50 and p95 block-application duration from the histogram, in milliseconds and separated by state_type.
panels.title: Block Apply Duration

panels.description: Extended per-step p95 gauges for bucket guard, consensus state machine and L1 apply phases. topk is evaluated per series, not statistically merged.
panels.title: Slowest Per-step P95

panels.description: Per-direction/per-port codec latency from latency_summaries/tcp_lz4. Requires --extended-metrics.
panels.title: TCP LZ4 Codec P95

panels.description: Codec duty cycle per direction and port. High sustained values indicate compression/decompression CPU pressure.
panels.title: TCP LZ4 Work Fraction

panels.description: New slow polls, long scheduling delays and dropped tasks over ten minutes. These are cumulative gauges, so delta is used and resets are clamped.
panels.title: Tokio Runtime Anomalies (10m)

panels.description: CPU seconds consumed per wall-clock second, expressed as CPU cores. Cumulative source resets are handled by rate and negative artifacts are clamped.
panels.title: Process CPU

panels.description: Resident memory for hl-node/hl-visor plus Go runtime system memory for the exporter.
panels.title: Memory

panels.description: Latest exponential moving average per validator. Requires validator latency files and should be compared within each observing instance.
panels.title: Slowest Validator Latency EMA

panels.description: Latest rounds-per-block sample and average QC round lag. Healthy rounds_per_block is usually near one.
panels.title: Consensus Round Health

panels.description: True counter rate of observed timeout rounds, grouped by suspect. Sustained non-zero activity indicates consensus instability.
panels.title: Timeout Round Rate

panels.description: Bottom validators by recent 100-block QC participation. The metric already represents percent and is network/observer specific.
panels.title: Lowest QC Participation

panels.description: Top validator HTTP response times in milliseconds. Requires validator RTT monitoring.
panels.title: Slowest Validator RTT

panels.description: New timeout-certificate rounds, catch-up events and dropped transactions. Source gauges reset with hl-node, so delta is clamped instead of rate.
panels.title: Consensus Anomalies (10m)

panels.description: Latest validator mempool size components. No data on non-validator nodes or when the mempool log source is absent.
panels.title: Mempool Depth

panels.description: Arrival and operation rates from data/mempool_txs. No data when split_client_blocks forwarding is not enabled end-to-end.
panels.title: Split-client Mempool Flow

panels.description: Actual filesystem usage percent, plus NODE_HOME and tmp footprints as bytes in separate panels below. Alerting should use filesystem usage, not directory size ratio.
panels.title: Filesystem Utilization

panels.description: Top NODE_HOME subdirectory sizes. Useful for identifying unbounded logs, replica commands, snapshots or database growth.
panels.title: Largest Node Subdirectories

panels.description: OS thread and open file-descriptor counts for hl-node and hl-visor. Watch for monotonic growth or sudden exhaustion patterns.
panels.title: Threads And Open FDs

panels.description: Current SST file count by database. Sustained growth can indicate compaction debt.
panels.title: RocksDB SST Files

panels.description: Current RocksDB block cache usage by database.
panels.title: RocksDB Block Cache

panels.description: New write stalls by database and reason. The source metric is a cumulative gauge; delta is clamped around source restarts.
panels.title: RocksDB Write Stalls (10m)

panels.description: Cumulative bug! and crit! events for hl-node/hl-visor. These gauges reset when the source process restarts; any bug! is page-level severity.
panels.title: Critical Messages Since Source Start

panels.description: Positive growth of cumulative bug!/crit! gauges over ten minutes. Negative restart resets are clamped to zero.
panels.title: New Critical Messages (10m)

panels.description: Top source file/line sites by cumulative critical count. Requires --extended-metrics and a node version that writes the rich critical-message file.
panels.title: Hot Critical Source Locations

panels.description: Rejected operator config sidecars, stale tmp files and pending shell output files. Non-zero failed loads require immediate configuration review.
panels.title: Operator And Temporary-file Anomalies

panels.description: Age of the latest replay event and of the latest successful periodic snapshot. Compare both pipelines independently; absence can be expected on nodes where a source is disabled.
panels.title: Replay And Snapshot Pipeline

panels.description: Age since each exporter monitor last completed a processing cycle. A growing series indicates a stuck monitor or missing source updates.
panels.title: Exporter Monitor Freshness

panels.description: New recovered monitor errors and panics over ten minutes. Both are true exporter-process counters and reset only when the exporter restarts.
panels.title: Exporter Monitor Failures (10m)

panels.description: Ages of independent exporter inputs. Compare sources rather than summing them; a single rising series identifies the stalled data pipeline.
panels.title: Input Data Freshness

panels.description: Optional active info-endpoint availability and response latency. Enable with --probe-info-endpoint; failures are a true counter.
panels.title: Info Endpoint Probe

title: Hyperliquid Node Operations
description: Operational dashboard for Hyperliquid node sync, abuse detection, P2P topology, latency, consensus, storage and exporter health.
